phrases.latin: In prīmō triviō, ut semper, dēlīberātum est. «Nōlō illāc īre, tata. Hāc eāmus!» «Fīat.»
phrases.english: At the first fork, as always, there was a debate. “I don’t want to go that way, Dad. Let’s go this way!” “All right.”

phrases.latin: hīc locus est, partīs ubi sē via findit in ambās: dextera quae Dītis magnī sub moenia tendit, hāc iter Ēlysium nōbīs; at laeva malōrum exercet poenās et ad impia Tartara mittit
phrases.english: this is the place where the road splits in two: the right-hand way, which runs under the walls of great Dis, is our road to Elysium; but the left one works the punishment of the wicked and sends them on to godless Tartarus

phrases.latin: ut ventum est in trivium, eādem quā cēterī fugere nōluit
phrases.english: when they came to the fork in the road, he refused to flee the same way as the rest

phrases.latin: Ubi via sē findit, ad dextram flectēmus.
phrases.english: Where the road forks, we’ll turn right.

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
